subject: Week 30: book the 9-month visit; regression window opens
bodyText:
This week
Pulling to stand at furniture is emerging for early movers, with the occasional sideways cruise step - the CDC checkpoint for both is 12 months, so absence means nothing. Babble now runs in long varied strings (bababa, mamama), and he is doing systematic physics: banging, dropping, and mouthing everything in reach. The motor surge often coincides with the 8/9-month sleep regression - night wakings to practice standing are skill-driven, not a schedule failure.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Standing in the crib and crying because he cannot get back down - teach sitting-back-down during daytime practice, and drop the mattress to its lowest setting.
- [monitor] No forward progress on any locomotion - no crawling, scooting, or rolling toward a target - worth documenting for the 9-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Any illness persisting past 3 days, or ear-pulling with fever.
- [call now] Labored breathing with retractions between the ribs, or fever at or above 102F (rectal) with lethargy - same-day call; 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness.

Enrichment opportunities
- Install hardware-mounted gates at the top of any stairs now rather than after the first climb - pressure-mounted passes only at the bottom - and lower the crib mattress the first day he pulls to stand.
- Hold the line on the existing sleep routine through the regression window - respond consistently, offer daytime standing practice, and resist introducing new sleep crutches; regressions resolve in 2-6 weeks when practices stay stable. AAP Getting Your Baby to Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Read 30+ minutes daily with longer pauses - treat his babble as a conversational turn and answer it; turn-taking, not word count alone, is what predicts language-network development. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Play crawling chase and rolling-ball games on the floor - locomotor play is the highest-value motor input this month, and it is free.

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18-Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit - influenza #2 if this is his first flu season, an iron rescreen, and possibly the ASQ-3 developmental screen. Book now; January pediatric slots compress around the holidays.
- Day 215-221 (week of Dec 12, 2026): furniture-anchoring audit - every tall piece, before cruising starts.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Responds to other people's emotional expressions
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Crying when a parent is sad, brightening when a parent laughs. Foundation of empathy.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-others-emotions/complete

- Distinguishes emotions by tone of voice
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Reacts differently to a stern vs warm voice with the same words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/distinguishes-emotion-tone/complete

- Finds a partially hidden object
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Beginning of object permanence — fully hidden objects come later.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/finds-partially-hidden-object/complete

- Struggles to reach objects that are out of reach
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Goal-directed behavior. Often precedes intentional rolling or scooting toward an object.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/struggles-for-out-of-reach/complete

- Begins to respond to the word 'no'
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Pauses briefly when the word is said. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-no/complete
